title: Comparison of ideal-data powers with recursive image powers
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $I$ ideal-sheaf data [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Let $(P_n,j_n)$ be its recursive image powers [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. For every $n\geq0$, the module attached to $I^n$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and there is an isomorphism $e:(I^n)^{\mathrm{mod}}\cong P_n$ with $j_n e=(I^n)^{\mathrm{mod}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$. The zeroth power is included.

source.place: Tags 01I8 and 01IC, affine quasi-coherent modules and tensor products; the affine ideal-product calculation used in Tag 01YB.

proof.text: The ideal module of any ideal-sheaf data is quasi-coherent: on each affine it is the tilde of the specified ideal. Recursive image powers have affine sections I(A)^n by the ideal-product formula, including the identity at n=0. Ideal-data powers have the same affine sections by their definition.

The two monomorphic inclusions have equal ranges on an affine basis, hence represent the same subsheaf of the structure module. The isomorphism between their monomorphic representatives commutes with the inclusions.

theorem idealData_recursive_power_comparison {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (n : ℕ) :
    (I ^ n).toModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ∃ e : (I ^ n).toModules ≅ (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).1,
        e.hom ≫ (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 = (I ^ n).toModulesι
